chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Safwan, from Umar ibn Riyah, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): 'When I arrive in Mecca, do I complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said: 'Complete it.' I said: 'And when I pass through Medina, do I complete the prayer or shorten it?' He said: 'Complete it.'

key_terms.إِتْمَامُ: Completing the prayer (four rak'ahs) instead of shortening it
key_terms.بِالْمَدِينَةِ: In Medina, the other major holy sanctuary
key_terms.تَقْصِيرُ: Shortening the four-rak'ah prayer to two rak'ahs

ai.seo_question: Do travelers shorten their prayers in Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the concession of *qasr* (shortening the four-rak'ah prayer) is suspended within the boundaries of the two holy sanctuaries, Mecca and Medina, requiring travelers to perform *tamam* (full four-rak'ah prayer). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes these specific cities from other places of travel, emphasizing their unique spiritual status where the traveler's temporary state does not diminish the completeness of worship. The dialogue format highlights the practical application of this rule for pilgrims moving between these sacred sites.
